content:
ashley: Heads up — deploy-bot queued the canary traffic split for the 02:00 UTC change window but approvals aren't moving. Anyone else seeing the approval queue stuck? :eyes:

mike: Yep saw it. UI shows 'pending approvals' even after clicking approve from the console.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: id=rb-2026-03-17-42, change_window=2026-03-18T02:00Z, approvals_required=2, approvals_received=0

tanvi: I approved from the console ~10:12 UTC, UI showed approved but deploy-bot still shows 2 pending. Might be an ack race between approval-service and scheduler.

jordan: Telemetry shows approval-svc latency spike -> webhook 504s around that time. I can see retries in the approval-service logs.

sre-bot: Alert: approval-service error rate > 5% (5m). Incident INC-6792 created.

ashley: Quick question: are approvals enforced at schedule time or execution time? Behavior affects whether late approvals are accepted.

mike: Current flow: schedule the rollout, deploy-bot records a schedule entry, final approval check runs at execution time. That allowed approvals to come in after scheduling but before the window. It was deliberate.

tanvi: If we change to pre-schedule enforcement we need to update the API/UI and last-minute approvals workflow. Some customers rely on late approvals for night windows.

jordan: Alternative idea: keep execution-time check but make deploy-bot re-query approvals with backoff if the approval endpoint times out during scheduling. That would hide transient webhook issues.

mike: Workaround for tonight: manual DB force-approve for rb-2026-03-17-42 (not ideal but unblocks).

ashley: Can we ship a small hotfix to deploy-bot to re-query approvals on scheduling failure? Something like: if approvals_received < required and time_until_window < 15m -> poll approvals endpoint 2-3 times with exponential backoff. Minimal surface area.

mike: I'll open a tiny PR with polling + metrics. Keep it feature-flagged so we can roll back if it misbehaves. Patch plan: poll up to 2 retries, 500ms -> 1s backoff, then proceed based on latest state. Deploy to staging, then prod.

deploy-bot: Note: simulated recheck may still report 0 if approval webhook acks are lost; ensure approval-service persists ack before reply.

tanvi: Also noticed another oddity: console rollout dashboard shows 0 canary traffic after traffic-start, but ingress logs show ~5% of requests routed to canary. Telemetry mapping might be missing route-id during rollout.

jordan: Filed TELE-312 to investigate mapping. Quick triage: add a chart on the rollout page that reads directly from ingress request logs (fast path) while telemetry mapping issue is fixed.

mike: PR opened: github.com/redwood/deploy-bot/pull/983 — adds the 2-retry polling behind flag `enable_approval_polling`. Will also emit metric `deploybot.approval_poll_retries`.

ashley: Great. Jordan/Tanvi — own TELE-312. Mike — ship the PR to staging and ping SRE once deployed. I'll pause any non-critical rollouts for tonight and update release notes. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: PagerDuty triggered for INC-6792 (approval-service latency). On-call: @sre-primary.

ashley: Example of deployment config we were trying to schedule (for context):

```yaml
rollout:
  id: rb-2026-03-17-42
  traffic_split:
    canary: 0.05
    main: 0.95
  guards:
    - name: latency
      threshold_ms: 400
    - name: error_rate
      threshold_pct: 0.5
```

mike: Heads up: if we change enforcement timing we also need to update the rollout API contract (clients rely on state transitions). Let's document in the PR.

jordan: I'll add a dashboard panel that cross-checks ingress logs vs telemetry so we can catch these mismatches early.

tanvi: After the hotfix, can we add an SLO for approval-ack latency? Right now we only track error-rate. A 1s 95p ack SLO would catch these.

ashley: Agreed. Add SLO proposal to the incident ticket. Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated when PR and staging deploy are live.
